panels.rationale: Single H&E histopathology panel (×10) from a skin biopsy in a case of pediatric pityriasis lichenoides chronica; the caption/in-text describe focal parakeratosis, multifocal vacuolar degeneration of the basal layer with lichenoid and superficial perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate, and pigmentary incontinence, and explicitly state these morphological findings suggested PLC. Panel is a real patient specimen showing histologic manifestations attributable to the target disease PLC.
panels.attribution_text: Ahmed et al. Pediatric Pityriasis Lichenoides Chronica, A Rare Case Report.. Clinical case reports 2026. doi:10.1002/ccr3.73331. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Histopathological examination of skin biopsy (Hematoxylin and Eosin [H&E] stain, ×10 magnification) showed slight acanthosis, focal parakeratosis, minimal, and multifocal vacuolar degeneration of the basal layer.
in_text_mentions: syphilis were negative, and HBSAg, complete blood count, LDH, AST, ALT, and ALK levels were unremarkable. Histopathological examination of skin biopsies showed slight acanthosis, focal parakeratosis, minimal and multifocal vacuolar degeneration of the basal layer, focal exocytosis of sparse lymphocytes, mild superficial perivascular and lichenoid lymphocytic infiltrates, and multifocal melanin‐laden macrophages with golden‐brown granules located both perivascularly and in other areas of the dermis (pigmentary incontinence) (Figure 2). The morphological findings suggested the diagnosis of PLC.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: H&E histopathology panel from a confirmed PLC case showing the classic lichenoid interface dermatitis with parakeratosis and necrotic keratinocytes, matching the captioned description. b: Lower-magnification H&E section from the same PLC biopsy demonstrating the lichenoid interface pattern described in the caption. c: Additional H&E field from the same PLC biopsy showing the captioned lichenoid interface dermatitis with necrotic keratinocytes.

in_text_mentions: Punch biopsy was performed (Figure 3), and the pathology report was consistent with PLC and was significant for hyperkeratosis, focal parakeratosis, and mild spongiosis. There is also lichenoid infiltrate of lymphocytes at the dermal–epidermal junction, and rare vacuoles and necrotic keratinocytes are identified (Figure 4).
